mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines a displacement reaction and distinguishes it from other types of reactions?

options.A: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal replaces a less reactive metal from its compound, forming a new metal and a new compound.
options.B: In a displacement reaction, two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds.
options.C: In a displacement reaction, a non‑metal replaces a metal in a compound.
options.D: In a displacement reaction, a metal reacts with water to produce hydrogen gas only.

mcqs.answer: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal replaces a less reactive metal from its compound, forming a new metal and a new compound.
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly describes a single displacement (or replacement) reaction, where a metal higher in the reactivity series displaces a metal lower in the series from its compound. Option B describes a double displacement reaction, Option C is not a standard classification, and Option D describes a specific reaction of some metals with water, not the general definition of displacement.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement (exchange) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: Option B shows the exchange of Na⁺ with Ag⁺, producing new compounds NaNO₃ and AgCl – a classic double displacement reaction. Option A is a single (metal) displacement, Option C is a combination reaction, and Option D is a decomposition reaction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions will produce a visible precipitate when the reactants are mixed in aqueous solution?
mcqs.explanation: Barium sulfate (BaSO₄) is insoluble in water, so its formation appears as a white precipitate. The other mixtures either produce soluble salts or gases that remain dissolved, resulting in no solid precipitate.

mcqs.question: A strip of zinc is placed in a solution of copper(II) sulfate. The solution gradually turns blue and metallic copper appears on the zinc strip. What type of reaction has taken place?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc, being more reactive than copper, displaces copper ions from CuSO₄, forming ZnSO₄ and elemental Cu. This is a classic single displacement reaction. It is not a double displacement because only one ion exchange occurs, nor is it decomposition or combustion.

mcqs.question: Statement: "Since magnesium reacts with dilute HCl, magnesium must be less reactive than iron, which does not react with dilute HCl." Is this statement correct?

options.B: No, the statement is false because magnesium is higher than iron in the reactivity series.
options.C: Yes, because both metals react with acids, they have the same reactivity.
options.D: No, the statement is false because only metals above hydrogen in the series react with acids.

mcqs.answer: No, the statement is false because magnesium is higher than iron in the reactivity series.
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium is placed above iron in the metal reactivity series, indicating it is more reactive. Therefore, the claim that magnesium is less reactive than iron is incorrect. Option D is partially true but does not directly address the comparison between Mg and Fe, making B the best answer.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Given the reactivity series K > Ca > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag > Au, which metal will be displaced when solid Zn is added to an aqueous solution of FeSO₄?

options.A: Iron will be displaced from FeSO₄.
options.B: Zinc will be displaced from FeSO₄.
options.D: Zinc will displace iron, forming ZnSO₄ and elemental iron.

mcqs.answer: Zinc will displace iron, forming ZnSO₄ and elemental iron.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than iron in the reactivity series, so it can displace iron from its compound. The reaction is Zn + FeSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Fe. Options A and B describe the opposite direction, and C ignores the reactivity relationship.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches each reaction with its type?

options.A: (i) Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂ → CaCO₃ + 2NaCl (double displacement); (ii) Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂ (single displacement)
options.B: (i) Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂ → NaCl + CaCO₃ (single displacement); (ii) Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂ (double displacement)
options.C: (i) Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂ → CaCO₃ + 2NaCl (single displacement); (ii) Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂ (double displacement)
options.D: (i) Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂ → CaCO₃ + 2NaCl (double displacement); (ii) Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂ (double displacement)

mcqs.answer: (i) Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂ → CaCO₃ + 2NaCl (double displacement); (ii) Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂ (single displacement)
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly identifies the first reaction as a double displacement (exchange of Na⁺ and Ca²⁺) and the second as a single (metal) displacement where Zn replaces H⁺. The other options misclassify one or both reactions.

mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, you are asked to select the reaction that will definitely produce a precipitate when the reactants are mixed in aqueous solution. Which reaction satisfies this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Barium sulfate (BaSO₄) is insoluble in water, so its formation results in a white precipitate, a common question in competitive exams. The other mixtures either produce soluble salts or gases that stay dissolved, yielding no solid precipitate.
